title: Oncall Evidence Collection and Reliability-Retro Playbook
author: Aditi Malhotra
content:
Summary
This runbook documents a standardized oncall evidence-collection workflow and post-incident retro standard tailored to SLO/error-budget lifecycle, capacity planning signals, reliability initiatives, and operational tooling at Redwood Inference. The goal is to reduce time-to-evidence, preserve high-fidelity telemetry, and produce actionable retros with clear remediation owners.

Scope
- Applicable to incidents that affect customer-facing inference endpoints (hosted API / dedicated) and core control plane services (routing, autoscaler, cache).
- Covers pre-incident instrumentation checks, oncall evidence collection, triage-to-retro handoff, and integration with capacity planning and reliability initiatives.

When to use this playbook
1) Any Sev2/Sev1 incident impacting availability, correctness, or latency SLOs.
2) Any sustained error-budget burn above 25% within a 7-day window (see Error budget triggers).
3) If capacity signals (queue depth, GPU util, pending pods) exceed thresholds in the Monitoring table.

Key definitions
- SLO: service-level objective defined for availability, latency, or correctness. Examples below.
- Error budget: 1 - SLO. Burn = observed violations vs allowed.
- Incident evidence: logs, spans, metrics, topology snapshot, deployment manifest, and oncall notes captured within the first 60 minutes.

SLO examples (production defaults)
- request_success_rate: 99.9% (rolling 30d)
- p95_latency_infer: 750ms (rolling 7d)
- p99_latency_controlplane: 300ms (rolling 30d)
- embedding_throughput_per_gpu: target 600 samples/s (steady-state)

Error budget burn thresholds and immediate actions
- 25% burn: Pager duty notify + primary oncall annotated timeline; review for mitigations.
- 50% burn: Trigger reliability-initiative triage meeting (weekly cadence) and notify product/ops.
- 80% burn: Lock new feature rollouts for the affected service; require explicit approval for deployments.
- 100% burn: Activate emergency capacity augmentation (see Capacity triggers), executive alert.

Monitoring & alert thresholds (operational table)
- metric | alert threshold | owner | immediate oncall action
- request_error_rate | >0.1% over 5m | api-service | escalate, capture traces
- p95_latency_infer | >750ms over 10m | inference-runtime | open degraded route, check batches
- gpu_utilization_per_pool | >85% 5m | gpu-fleet | scale capacity request, apply surge policy
- pending_requests_queue_length | >500 | routing-service | enable fallback routing to warm pool
- cache_kv_hit_rate | <70% 15m | cache-service | inspect TTL and eviction patterns

Pre-incident instrumentation checklist (runbook step 0)
- Confirm alerting is up: curl -sS https://alertmanager.internal/api/v1/status || report to SRE-tooling.
- Ensure critical dashboards are bookmarked: API health, Inference latency, GPU pool utilization, Queue depth.
- Verify correct retention windows: metrics 90d, traces 30d, logs 30d (compressed) unless otherwise specified.

Oncall evidence-collection procedure (first 0-60 minutes)
1) Triage and annotate timeline (0-5m): create incident post in Incident Tracker and fill short description, services impacted, and initial hypothesis. Use template: "Impact: X% customers, symptom: increased 5xx/errors or high latency, start: <timestamp>".
2) Attach topology snapshot (0-10m): run infra snapshot-helper to capture current deployments + image tags + node pool state. Command:
- ./tools/snapshot-helper --services api,routing,inference --output /tmp/incident-{{TIMESTAMP}}.tar.gz
3) Snapshot metrics and traces (0-15m): export time-windowed queries to incident storage. Recommended PromQL and tracing queries:
- Prometheus query (5m window): sum(rate(http_requests_total{job=\"api\",status!~\"2..\"}[5m])) by (status)
- Latency rollup: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Traces: open tracing link for top 25 sampled traces with status=error; attach trace IDs to incident.
4) Capture logs (0-30m): run filtered retrieval for the timeframe + 5 minutes before incident start. Example Loki/ELK query:
- json | service:inference-runtime AND (level:ERROR OR status:5..) | earliest: -10m until +10m
- Persist ACL-safe copies to incident bucket: gsutil cp -r <results> gs://redwood-incidents/{{INCIDENT_ID}}/evidence/logs/
5) Resource state (0-20m): collect kubectl/k8s state and GPU metrics:
- kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --show-labels > /tmp/pods-{{TIMESTAMP}}.txt
- nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/gpu-{{POOL}}-{{TIMESTAMP}}.xml (where accessible)
6) Configuration and recent changes (0-30m): attach recent deploys (git SHAs), autoscaler events, config changes. CLI examples:
- git log --since='1 day ago' --pretty=oneline --grep=\"deploy\" apps/inference
- gcloud container clusters describe <cluster> --format json > /tmp/cluster.json
7) Initial mitigation notes (0-60m): record any immediate fixes (rollback, routing change, scale up) and exact commands used (for reproducibility) in the incident timeline.

Evidence preservation rules
- Never delete raw artifacts. Compress and store evidence in incident bucket with retention tag incident_evidence:30d.
- Redact customer data inside logs before sharing externally; follow data-management policy.
- Tag evidence with SLO impact labels: slo:availability, slo:latency, slo:correctness.

Triage: mapping to SLOs and error budgets (first 1-4 hours)
1) Identify which SLOs were affected and compute the burn for the incident window. Use standard burn calculation script:
- ./tools/calc-error-budget --slo request_success_rate --window 1h --from <start> --to <end>
2) If burn >50% escalate to Reliability Initiatives channel and create a dedicated task in the reliability backlog.
3) If latency SLO affected, attach detailed pXX plots and top contributing endpoints to the incident.

Post-incident retro standard (within 72 hours)
- Required deliverables: Incident timeline, root cause hypothesis, evidence bundle link, remediation plan (owner + ETA), SLO impact statement including error budget delta, and lessons learned.
- Structured retro template:
  - Why it happened (root cause summary)
  - How it was detected (alerts/observability)
  - What we did (mitigation steps)
  - What failed in our process (instrumentation, playbooks, permissions)
  - Action items (owner, ETA, verification criteria)
- Timebox: publish draft retro within 72 hours, finalize within 14 days after validation.
- Retro review: required signoff by service owner, SRE lead, and product owner for changes that affect rollout policy.

Reliability initiatives and remediation scoring
- Use a simple impact/effort score to prioritize: impact (1-5) x effort (1-5). Focus on >8 combined score.
- Typical initiatives: autoscaler tuning, prefix caching expansion, model quantization trial for hot endpoints, warm pool sizing, alert suppression fixes.
- Each initiative must include verification criteria: SLO delta improvement, cost delta estimate, and rollout plan.

Capacity planning integration
- After incidents that tie to capacity, add a dedicated capacity request item to quarterly capacity board: include observed peak, recommended headroom, and expected cost.
- Headroom guidance: target steady-state GPU util 60-70% with 20% warm pool for burst; scale rules should maintain average queue latency under 200ms.
- Use backlog tags: capacity:urgent or capacity:normal to triage.

Operational tooling checklist and examples
- Incident creation: ./tools/create-incident --service inference --severity sev2 --summary \"<short>\"
- Evidence snapshot helper (see above).
- Error budget calc: ./tools/calc-error-budget --slo p95_latency_infer --window 24h
- Dashboards: link names - \"Inference: Latency Heatmap\", \"GPU Pools: Utilization & Queues\", \"API: Error Breakdown by Status\".
- Automation recommendations: instrument runbook steps 2-5 to trigger automatically when an incident is paged (proof-of-concept implemented in incident-automation repo).

Ownership & escalation matrix
- Primary oncall: first responder, evidence collection, immediate mitigation.
- Service owner: decision authority for rollbacks and canary freezes.
- SRE lead: coordinates retro and reliability scoring.
- Capacity owner (gpu-fleet): executes reserved capacity requests and surge policies.

Verification and closure criteria
- All evidence artifacts uploaded and linked in incident record.
- Retro doc published with assigned action items and verification steps.
- Error budget delta calculated and added to SLO dashboard.
- If remediation touches infra/config, require canary with health checks for 24h and then close action.

Appendix: sample queries and snippets
- Prometheus: sum(increase(requests_total{job=\"api\",status=\"5xx\"}[5m]))
- Loki: {app=\"inference-runtime\"} | json | status = \"500\" | line_format \"{timestamp} {message}\"
- kubectl: kubectl get hpa -n inference -o wide
- Example incident create: ./tools/create-incident --service routing --severity sev1 --summary \"regional 5xx spike\" --assignees @oncall

Related pages and artifacts
- Incident automation repo: git+ssh://git.redwood/repo/incident-automation
- SLO catalog: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/slo-catalog-2025

Notes and evolving practices
- This playbook is intended to be concise and executable; teams should add service-specific extraction queries to the \"evidence snippets\" section in their service wiki.
- We expect iterative improvements: automate snapshot-helper, add more error-budget wheels to dashboards, and integrate GPU warm pool actions into the autoscaler.

Appendix: checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Create incident record and annotate timeline
- [ ] Run snapshot-helper and upload tarball
- [ ] Export Prometheus queries and traces to incident storage
- [ ] Collect pods/node/gpu state and save
- [ ] Attach last 24h of deploys and config changes
- [ ] Compute error budget burn and label incident accordingly
- [ ] Draft retro within 72h, finalize and assign actions
